papers.title: SEC: One-Share Everywhere-Short Secret Sharing from Lossless Expanders
papers.abstract: We introduce SEC, an expander-code-based ramp secret sharing scheme over $\mathbb{Z}$-modules, particularly suitable for lattice-based distributed cryptography. It is everywhere-short: bounded secret coefficients yield bounded share coefficients, and the integer reconstruction vectors have bounded entries. Moreover, each participant receives exactly one share, regardless of the number of parties and the privacy and reconstruction thresholds. This improves on prior schemes with bounded share coefficients and bounded entries in the integer reconstruction vectors, in which the number of sub-shares or shares per participant grows either with the number of parties and the threshold or with the security parameter. The construction rests on a coding-theoretic observation: in the bi-adjacency matrix of a lossless bipartite expander, unique-neighbor peeling completes every sufficiently small set of columns to a square unimodular submatrix. We prove correctness, everywhere-shortness, and linearity, and give a publicly computable entrywise bound on the reconstruction vector our algorithm returns for each authorized set. For privacy, we introduce hard-core local leakage resilience, which strengthens the leakage-resilience notion of Nielsen and Simkin (EUROCRYPT 2020) to protect a hard-core function of the secret, and we prove that SEC satisfies it against correlated multi-query local leakage under the MatrixHint-MLWE problem, which admits a reduction from the standard MLWE problem. For $n=60$ participants and security parameter $\kappa=128$, SEC achieves privacy threshold 6 against $2^{64}$ leakage queries and empirical reconstruction threshold 46. The ideal entropy-coded secret and share sizes are about 3.5 KiB and 6.4 KiB, respectively.

papers.title: Affine Combiners for Reed-Solomon Proximity Gaps
papers.abstract: Reed-Solomon proximity gaps establish soundness guarantees for protocols that test received words through random combinations. For length-$n$ codes over $\mathbb{F}_q$, classical scalar combiners achieve error $O(n/q)$ in the unique-decoding regime, with larger known bounds near the Johnson radius. We prove smaller error bounds using affine combiners, which combine two received words $f,g$ as $f(x)+(\alpha+\beta x)g(x)$, where $\alpha,\beta$ are independent uniform elements of $\mathbb{F}_q$. For output degree bound $d=\rho n$, fixed $\rho\in(0,1)$ and $0<\eta<1-\sqrt{\rho}$, and sufficiently large block length $n$, we prove mutual correlated agreement (MCA) with one coordinate of agreement loss at threshold $A=\lceil(\sqrt{\rho}+\eta)n\rceil$, with error $O_{\rho,\eta}\left(\frac{1}{q}+\frac{n^2}{q^2}\right)$. The result holds over arbitrary evaluation domains in every finite field, including prime and binary extension fields. The agreement threshold can approach the Johnson threshold, beyond unique decoding. For $q\ge n^2$, our error is $O_{\rho,\eta}(1/q)$, an asymptotic factor-$n$ separation from scalar combiners: we prove that their worst-case MCA error is $\Omega_{\rho,\eta}(n/q)$ at the same agreement threshold and with the same one-coordinate loss. We also prove that affine combiners incur worst-case error $\Omega_{\rho,\eta}(n/q)$ when no agreement loss is allowed. Thus one coordinate of agreement loss is necessary for our guarantee; this relaxation of standard MCA reduces the guaranteed common agreement fraction by at most $1/n$. We also extend the result to $k$-variate Reed-Muller codes on subfield grids, obtaining MCA error $O_{\rho,\eta,k}(q^{-k})$ for fixed $\rho,\eta,k$, sufficiently large $n$, and $q\ge n^{k+1}$, with agreement loss $n^{1-1/k}$.

papers.title: Optimal Additive Integer Masks for One-Guess Vulnerability under an Absolute-Moment Budget
papers.abstract: We study the average one-guess success probability of an adversary who observes the ordinary integer sum of a finite-support secret and an independent integer-valued mask, subject to an absolute-moment budget on the mask. For a uniform secret on an interval the exact optimum and an explicit optimiser are obtained. For a biased bit the masks that achieve no increase over the prior baseline are characterised and their minimal cost is determined. The entire cost-vulnerability frontier is then determined for every bias. It is the piecewise-linear interpolation of an explicit sequence of points generated by cost-optimally shifted truncated geometric masks. It has infinitely many affine pieces, which accumulate at the critical cost, where the frontier meets the prior baseline with zero slope. The proof rests on a layer-cake decomposition of an arbitrary mask into truncated geometrics, along which both the vulnerability and the cost are exactly additive. The results give exact design guidance for additive integer noise under the average one-guess metric; they do not constitute a cryptographic masking scheme.

papers.title: Context Graph: Explainable Multi-Agent Decision Chains in AI-RAN
papers.abstract: AI-RAN distributes network control across multiple autonomous agents, namely xApps and rApps operating over shared radio resources. When an alert or degradation appears, operators currently lack a structured way to trace which decision caused it, what context triggered that decision, and how other agents interacted. Existing explainability tools focus on single-model feature attribution or linear event logging, neither of which captures cross-agent decision chains. We propose the Context Graph, a heterogeneous directed graph that organizes policies, measurements, decisions, and alerts into a queryable explanation layer. Its foundational primitive is the Decision-Event node acting as a causal junction, where incoming edges capture triggering context and outgoing edges track downstream consequences that are progressively upgraded through counterfactual verification. Instantiated over existing E2, A1, and O1 data flows, our proof-of-concept demonstrates that compliance and diagnosis queries are resolved at sub-millisecond latency over graphs of tens of thousands of nodes, while reliably distinguishing true causal impacts from spurious correlations.

papers.title: LazyWeights: Decode-on-Demand Edge LLMs
papers.abstract: Memory decides which LLMs an edge device runs, and how fast: capacity on a $4$ GB Jetson Nano, bandwidth on an $8$ GB Jetson Orin Nano Super. Deployed formats (GPTQ, AWQ, $\texttt{llama.cpp}$'s K- and I-quants) spend equal bits on every integer code of a matrix, although the codes are far from uniform. $\texttt{LazyWeights}$ keeps these formats but tunes GPTQ so the codes compress, Huffman-codes them losslessly in interleaved lanes, and decodes them on demand in a small unit between DRAM and L2, so GPU kernels run unchanged and DRAM moves only coded bytes. At $1\%$ and $3.5\%$ perplexity budgets, coded Phi-3-mini, Mistral-7B and SmolLM-1.7B are $5.7-31.4\%$ smaller than the best $\texttt{llama.cpp}$ format. A bit-exact $0.21$ mm$^2$ ASIC decoder unit ($1$ GHz, $7$ nm) cuts Orin latency and energy per token by up to $36\%$ and $38\%$ ($54\%$ and $44\%$ with prompt-lookup speculation). On the Nano, $\texttt{LazyWeights}$ needs $58-64\%$ less time and $53-57\%$ less energy per token than CPU $\texttt{llama.cpp}$, and runs a streamed Mistral-7B 6.6$\times$ faster at $3.89$ bits per weight. A Huffman decoder beats an rANS decoder in rate and area at equal throughput; the ASIC decoder unit runs bit-exact on a Zynq UltraScale+ FPGA (AMD ZCU102).

papers.title: Shannon observables: A scalable approach to information decomposition
papers.abstract: Distributed systems, such as biological and artificial neural networks, process information via complex interactions engaging multiple subsystems, resulting in high-order structure of the information within the system with distinct properties across scales. Investigating how these systems process information remains challenging due to difficulties in defining appropriate multivariate metrics and ensuring their scalability to large systems. To address these challenges, we introduce a novel framework based on what we call "Shannon observables": quantities that capture essential properties of high-order information processing, yet can be computed directly from Shannon entropies and scale efficiently to large systems. Our theoretical results demonstrate how Shannon observables can be used to resolve long-standing ambiguities regarding the interpretation of widely used multivariate information-theoretic measures. On the practical side, we demonstrate the framework's versatility across several domains. An analytical study of error-correcting codes shows how Shannon observables trace out distinct encoding regimes as channel noise varies; analyses of deep classifiers and convolutional autoencoders reveal characteristic information-processing signatures across layers and over training; and applied to magnetoencephalography recordings from the human brain, the framework yields a cortical atlas exposing pronounced regional structure in directed information transfer. Overall, our framework resolves fundamental limitations in analysing high-order information phenomena and offers broad opportunities for theoretical developments and empirical analyses.

papers.title: Explicit Subspace Evasive Sets via Subspace Designs
papers.abstract: Given a finite field $\mathbb F_q$, we say that a set $A\subseteq \mathbb F^n_q$ is an $(r,c)$ subspace evasive set if and only if for any affine subspace $U\subseteq \mathbb F^n_q$ with bounded dimension $\dim(U)\leq r$, the intersection size $|A\cap U|$ is at most $c$. The probabilistic method shows the existence of $(r,c)$ subspace evasive sets with $|A| = q^{(1-\epsilon) n}$ with $c = O(r/\epsilon)$. However, the best explicit constructions by Dvir--Lovett (STOC 2012) and Ben-Aroya--Shinkar (CJTCS 2013) have $c$ growing as an exponential function of $r$. Here, we give an explicit construction of such subspace evasive set that achieves the intersection bound $c=O(\min(r\log(r/\epsilon)/\epsilon, r^2/\epsilon))$ when both $r$ and $1/\epsilon$ are constants. Our approach is simple and the key idea is to compose subspace design codes (Guruswami-Xing, STOC 2013) with a suitably chosen ``local'' subspace evasive set. As a corollary, we give the first construction of an explicit (strongly) capacity-achieving list-recoverable code with nearly optimal list size, circumventing all previously-known barriers to construction.

papers.title: Explicit Edit Codes via Multicoloring
papers.abstract: For any fixed integers $q\ge2$ and $t\ge1$, we construct explicit $q$-ary codes of length $n$ that correct any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions, and substitutions, with redundancy at most $2t\log_q n+O_{q,t}(\log\log n)$ $q$-ary symbols. This matches the leading redundancy term of Levenshtein's classical existential bound. Building on the standard graph-coloring approach, we use a prime-based multicoloring of the edit-confusion graph to assign multiple colors to each $q$-ary word of length $m<n$. Appending a short, edit-protected representation of an assigned color to the length-$m$ word yields a length-$n$ codeword. The choice among the assigned colors carries additional message information, thereby reducing the redundancy. The construction admits deterministic encoding and decoding in $\widetilde O_{q,t}(n^{6t+2})$ and $\widetilde O_{q,t}(n^{7t+2})$ time, respectively.

papers.title: Generalized Bicycle Codes with Low Connectivity: Minimum Distance Bounds and Competitive Circuit-Level Performance
papers.abstract: We present new upper and lower bounds on the minimum distance of certain generalized bicycle (GB) codes that go beyond the capabilities of techniques based on classical codes. These bounds are shown to capture the true minimum distance for specific subclasses within the GB family. In particular, we demonstrate the existence of two highly degenerate GB code families with parameters $[\![d^2+1,2,d]\!]_2$ for odd $d \geq 3$ and $[\![d^2,2,d]\!]_2$ for even $d \geq 4$, both having qubit connectivity of four, similar to that of surface codes. For the odd-distance family, we analyze the structure of low-weight logical Pauli operators and establish the existence of a fault-tolerant logical CNOT gate between the two logical qubits, achievable via a simple relabeling of data qubits. Next, using nearly self-inverse polynomials, we extend our results to construct an infinite class of connectivity-six GB codes with an improved rate. For GB codes based on these polynomials, we further present a technique to realize transversal logical CNOT gates via data-qubit permutations. We further construct syndrome extraction schemes for our connectivity four GB families that avoid reductions in minimum distance due to circuit-level faults propagating from check qubits to data qubits. Finally, we numerically evaluate the logical error rate performance of the mentioned connectivity four families of GB codes under circuit-level noise, obtaining thresholds comparable to those of rotated surface codes.

papers.title: ComBO: Community Bayesian Optimization for Carrier Shutdown in HAPS-Hypercell Networks
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate carrier shutdown (CS) in high-altitude platform station (HAPS)-Hypercell-assisted networks, leveraging network-wide information to optimize both coverage macro cells and capacity cells CS. To address the high dimensionality of this problem, we propose ComBO, a community-aware Bayesian optimization framework that exploits user equipment (UE) reference signal received power (RSRP) reports to construct a fallback graph representing the underlying network and identify groups of strongly coupled cells. The resulting communities decompose the original optimization problem into lower-dimensional subproblems, which are sequentially optimized using trust region Bayesian optimization (TuRBO) and refined through a final joint search. Evaluation in a high-fidelity 3GPP-based system-level environment shows that ComBO consistently outperforms legacy CS strategies and overcomes the scalability limitations of global Bayesian optimization (BO). Considering normalized terrestrial power ComBO achieves nearly 84% savings while preserving quality of service. These results demonstrate the potential of community-aware decomposition as a scalable approach to large-scale network optimization.

papers.title: Message-Passing-Based Bayesian Joint Channel Estimation and Data Detection for Pilot-Guard-Free AFDM
papers.abstract: Existing channel estimation methods for affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) over doubly dispersive channels commonly isolate pilots and data with pilot guard symbols, resulting in substantial transmission overhead, while fractional Doppler introduces off-grid mismatch and complicates accurate channel estimation. This paper develops a pilot-guard-free AFDM transmission and reception scheme with a Bayesian receiver for joint channel estimation and data symbol detection. Uniformly interleaved pilots are embedded among data symbols without dedicated guard symbols, and the resulting pilot-data coupling is explicitly incorporated into the joint inference problem rather than suppressed through guard-based isolation.

papers.title: Reduced-Complexity WMMSE Approach for Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems With Finite-Capacity Fronthaul Links
papers.abstract: We propose a reduced-complexity weighted minimum mean squared error (R-WMMSE) framework for cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) systems with finite-capacity fronthaul links. To maximize the system capacity, we need to jointly design beamforming vectors at distributed access points (APs) and fronthaul quantization noise covariances. Such a task would be addressed using conventional WMMSE algorithms and their variants. However, existing WMMSE-based methods either assume ideal infinite-capacity fronthaul links or incur high computational complexity when jointly optimizing the network-wide beamforming and fronthaul compression variables. To this end, the proposed method jointly optimizes beamforming and fronthaul compression by leveraging a sequential per-AP optimization strategy. Since each subproblem is efficiently solved via Lagrangian duality with closed-form updates, the overall computational complexity can be significantly reduced compared to the conventional WMMSE method. To further reduce hardware cost, we extend the R-WMMSE framework to hybrid analog-digital beamforming systems, tackling the joint design of digital beamforming, fronthaul compression, and analog beamforming. Numerical results show that the proposed scheme achieves performance nearly identical to that of the conventional WMMSE while reducing the runtime by over 99%.

papers.title: Hybrid Precoding and Combining for O-RAN Massive MIMO Systems
papers.abstract: Recently, the radio access network (RAN) has been reimagined through open RAN (O-RAN) architecture to overcome the limitations of the traditional monolithic, black-box design philosophy and to leverage emerging technologies such as cloud computing, machine learning, and artificial intelligence. Although O-RAN disaggregates the base station (BS) into independent components to enable modular deployment, this paradigm introduces new challenges in signal processing and beamforming. In particular, beamforming in O-RAN must account for fronthaul link (FHL) capacity constraints, coordinated operation of multiple radio units (possibly from different vendors), and resource management, including transmit power allocation. To address these challenges, this work proposes novel beamforming techniques for a downlink multiuser hybrid massive multiple-input multiple-output system, in which hybrid architectures are deployed at both the users and at each BS radio unit. We formulate a sum-rate maximization problem incorporating transmit-power, unit-modulus, and FHL capacity constraints. The proposed algorithm integrates gradient descent and the Lagrange multiplier method to design analog beamformers and digital precoders, respectively, whereas digital combiners are designed to render the received streams parallel to each other. By avoiding computationally intensive operations such as eigenvalue and singular value decompositions, the proposed approach, as evidenced by simulation results, achieves superior performance with moderate computational complexity compared to existing benchmark schemes.

papers.title: Multimodal Semantic Communication using Shared and Unique Representation Decomposition
papers.abstract: Semantic communication (SemCom) has emerged as a promising paradigm for bandwidth-constrained mobile and vehicular networks. This paper proposes a unified representation learning framework for multimodal SemCom (MSC), which encodes heterogeneous data into a compact semantic space for efficient transmission and source recovery. The framework addresses the multimodal semantic representation gap, which arises when at least one modality contains semantic information that cannot be fully inferred from the other. To preserve this information for reconstruction, the framework decomposes each representation into shared and modality-specific components. We formulate a mutual information objective for source reconstruction, cross-modal alignment of the shared components, and decoupling of the shared and modality-specific components. To enhance transmission efficiency, we introduce a shared knowledge base implemented as a compact codebook of semantic vectors learned during training. The shared components are transmitted digitally as codebook indices, while the modality-specific components are sent in analog form. We apply knowledge distillation during training, using a pretrained vision foundation model to guide the learning of quantized shared features. On image--text pairs over additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) and Extended Vehicular A (EVA) channels, the proposed framework improves image reconstruction over conventional separate source-channel coding (SSCC) and representative multimodal and unimodal SemCom systems. Further evaluations show gradual degradation under channel-estimation mismatch, complementary effects of alignment, decoupling, and knowledge distillation on the shared representation, and alignment of shared features across modalities with separation of the modality-specific features.

papers.title: MetaCom: Meta Codebook Learning for Robust V2X Semantic Communications
papers.abstract: Collaborative perception in Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) networks faces dual challenges: strictly limited bandwidth and channel impairments. Existing static quantization schemes often suffer from feature manifold drift caused by highly non-stationary traffic environments. To address this, we propose MetaCom, a robust digital semantic communication framework featuring a Meta-Codebook Learning paradigm. First, we introduce a Differentiable Quantized Semantic Communications (DQSemCom) module trained with perturbations induced by the simulated digital modulation and channel via Gumbel-Softmax relaxation. Building on this, we design a Bi-Level Meta-Evolution Mechanism (Bi-MEM) that treats manifold drift as a sequence of rapid adaptation tasks, aligning the codebook via data-level smoothing and parameter-level meta-updates. Furthermore, we validate MetaCom under AWGN, Rayleigh, and Rician fading channels. Experimental results demonstrate that MetaCom achieves superior trade-offs between perception precision and communication overhead, outperforming state-of-the-art methods by a significant margin under low-SNR conditions.

papers.title: VR-Net: Subarray-Level Inter-Cell Coordination for Multi-Cell XL-MIMO under Near-Field Spatial Non-Stationarity
papers.abstract: Spatial non-stationarity in multi-cell extremely large-scale MIMO (XL-MIMO) confines each user to a visibility region (VR) of each array. VR-Net exploits these regions for subarray-level coordinated beamforming. A base-station (BS)-indexed conflict graph identifies overlapping VRs; gain-based association and a masked multi-cell weighted minimum mean square error (WMMSE) iteration restrict beam design and channel state information (CSI) uploads to the relevant subarray blocks. We establish conditions for exact per-cell decoupling, derive the expected CSI loads, bound the loss of designing on the VR-gated channel and the loss of the support constraint, and characterize single-edge visibility contrast through a closed-form Fresnel transition width. Simulations use a 3GPP TR 38.901 Release-19-based near-field UMi channel with modular facade arrays and pre-registered criteria. At a 30 dB threshold, VR-Net retains at least 99.6% of the full-aperture WMMSE sum rate in every tested setting while uploading 10-39% fewer complex CSI entries. It gains up to 3.5 bit/s/Hz over an all-user adaptation of the multi-cell scheme of P\'erez-Ad\'an et al. at moderate power and dense load, and inter-cell coordination adds up to 33% over per-cell design.

papers.title: Rateless Coding for Efficient Model Broadcast in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Model broadcast in federated learning (FL) with wireless channels faces significant challenges due to large model sizes and heterogeneous, unreliable channel conditions. While rateless coding has been widely adopted in modern broadcast communications to handle channel heterogeneity, its potential for model broadcast in FL remains largely unexplored. To fill this gap, we propose a joint source-channel coding scheme based on rateless coding to improve the robustness and efficiency of downlink model broadcast in FL. Specifically, we establish a rigorous convergence analysis of FL to inform the rateless code and quantization design under noisy downlink channel conditions. Moreover, by observing that the iterative process of FL naturally provides prior information about client updates, we leverage client-side local models as conditional prior information to aid the decoding process, thereby reducing transmission costs. Extensive simulations demonstrate that our rateless coding scheme significantly enhances downlink model broadcast efficiency in FL, while retaining comparable training accuracies for both homogeneous and heterogeneous data distributions.

papers.title: An Empirical Square-Root Law for the Degree Discrepancy of Binary m-Sequences
papers.abstract: Let $k\ge 2$, $N=2^k$, $M=N-1$ and let $\Delta(r)$ be the range, over all starting offsets, of the total-variation degree discrepancy of a length-$r$ window of a primitive binary linear feedback shift register (LFSR) of period $M$. Degree-discrepancy profiles for every $k\le 28$ support the scaling $\max_r \Delta(r)=\Theta(\sqrt{N})=\Theta(2^{k/2})$. The tabulated peaks are maxima on a discrete grid, hence lower bounds on the exhaustive maximum. The normalized peaks $d_k=\max_{r\in R_k}\Delta(r)/2^{k/2}$ oscillate between values near 1/2 and values that approach, but do not exceed, 1. The data suggest $\liminf d_k=1/2$ and $\limsup d_k\le 1$. We conjecture the same square-root law for the exhaustive maximum, with those normalized envelopes. A Brownian-bridge heuristic accounts for the square-root scale. The same profiles do not place the recorded maximizer at mid-path: after folding by the complement identity $\Delta(M-r)=\Delta(r)$, the median of $\min(\rho^*_k,1-\rho^*_k)$ is 0.35, and several $k$ (notably 16 and 28) peak on a short window. Mid-horizon $\Delta$ remains a large fraction of the peak, so the square-root scale can still come from a Brownian-bridge envelope. The same range has two readings of the starting offset: a pairing fragment in serial-knockout scheduling, and a change to the plaintext on an LFSR orbit. The location of the maximizer is not part of the conjecture. Open questions that separate the conjecture from a theorem are listed.

papers.title: Optimization of Finite Alphabet Message Passing Decoding on Fully Node-Parallel Architectures for 5G LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel design method for the lookup tables (LUTs) of the minimum reconstruction, computation, and quantization (min-RCQ) LDPC code decoding algorithm. The proposed design method uses Bayesian optimization and samples from a subspace of the design space. The novel design method does not require knowledge about the channel or the modulation format and uses the frame error rate (FER) as loss function. The design method is applicable to irregular low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes with puncturing and shortening. Furthermore, the design method creates a set of iteration-agnostic LUTs that can be used over all iterations, which makes this approach suitable for fully node-parallel decoder architectures. We show that our proposed approach achieves a 38.6 % better energy efficiency than a state-of-the-art normalized min-sum (NMS) decoder without loss in error correction performance.

papers.title: Closed-Form Gaussian Information Projection for Embedded Hypercubes and Beta--Gaussian Mixtures
papers.abstract: We derive closed-form Gaussian information projections of Beta--Gaussian distributions whose tangential components are supported on affine embedded hypercubes and whose normal components are Gaussian. The optimal Gaussian is uniquely characterized by moment matching, and the corresponding minimum Kullback--Leibler divergence admits an explicit expression depending only on the intrinsic Beta parameters, independently of the embedding geometry, ambient dimension, and normal Gaussian parameters. In the uniform case, this divergence reduces to a linear function of the intrinsic dimension. We further extend this construction to finite, pure embedded cubical complexes by considering mixtures of the componentwise Gaussian projections. Using the joint convexity of the Kullback--Leibler divergence, we establish an explicit upper bound on the approximation error of the resulting Gaussian Mixture. For uniform tangential distributions and volume-based mixture weights, the bound is linear in the intrinsic dimension and independent of the geometry of the complex, its embedding, and the normal Gaussian parameters.

papers.title: Two-Stage Secret Sharing
papers.abstract: We give an information-theoretic formulation of two-stage secret sharing for situations in which secret information becomes available progressively. In the proposed model, shares for an initial part of the secret are distributed before the remaining part becomes available, and additional shares are distributed to new participants after the remaining part becomes available, without updating the shares already distributed and without using any additional information other than shares. To characterize this setting, we propose the notion of a two-stage access structure and provide its characterization. We further quantify the amount of information about the first-stage secret that the dealer must retain between the two distribution stages, derive a universal lower bound, and present a construction that achieves this bound for every two-stage access structure. We also position advance sharing as a special case of the proposed model and give its characterization and a related construction in classical information-theoretic secret sharing.

papers.title: Concatenated Codes with One Inner Code: Low-Rate Gilbert-Varshamov Asymptotics from Algebraic-Geometric Codes
papers.abstract: Constructing codes that attain the Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound while admitting efficient encoding and decoding is a fundamental problem in coding theory. We study concatenated codes that reuse a single binary inner code across all outer coordinates. To exploit existing encoding and decoding algorithms, we restrict the outer codes to random subcodes of scaled copies of prescribed algebraic codes and investigate their minimum distance. Our first contribution is a general upper bound on the minimum-distance failure probability that separates two terms controlled by the inner code's bias moments and the dual weight distribution of the prescribed code, together with sufficient conditions for exponential decay. Our second contribution is a concrete construction satisfying these conditions using algebraic-geometric codes from the Garcia-Stichtenoth tower. For every sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$, we construct a family of random binary codes $C_m$ whose rates approach $\varepsilon^2$ and satisfy \[ \Pr\left[\delta(C_m)\geq\frac12-\sqrt{\frac{\ln 2}{2}}\left(\varepsilon+\frac{\varepsilon^3}{2}\right)\right]\geq 1-2^{-c\varepsilon^4N_m}, \] for all sufficiently large $m$, where $N_m$ is the block length and $c>0$ is independent of $\varepsilon$ and $m$. Thus, the distance guarantee matches the leading coefficient of the GV bound at low rates. For each fixed $\varepsilon$, the construction uses a single inner encoding map throughout the family and admits polynomial-time encoding and unique decoding within a guaranteed radius. This answers the question of Doron, Mosheiff, and Wootters for subcodes of scaled algebraic geometry codes at low rates.

papers.title: A Constructive Theory of Closed-Form Rate-Distortion Functions
papers.abstract: Rate-distortion functions are defined by a variational problem whose analytic solution depends on the source distribution and distortion measure. We develop a posterior-based construction framework using conditional entropy as a common distortion coordinate. Building on the rate-entropy formulation, we establish entropy-level attainability for discrete sources with finite entropy and absolutely continuous sources with integrable log densities. We give a constructive rate-entropy coding proof for finite-alphabet sources and such continuous sources, without a second-moment assumption. Marginal compatibility ensures that a candidate posterior and output distribution recover the source, while a Gibbs representation and a kernel mass bound certify attainment of maximum conditional entropy. The negative log posterior identifies candidate fixed distortions. Excess rate equals a conditional entropy gap and decomposes into budget slack and posterior mismatch. Convolution decompositions and conjugate posteriors provide two construction paths. They recover established results, including the Gamma-source rate-distortion function under Itakura-Saito distortion, and yield a closed-form parametric expression for zeta sources under divisibility-constrained logarithmic multiplicative distortion. Exact expressions are obtained on specified intervals for negative binomial sources under one-sided counting distortion and Gamma sources under one-sided mean error. A residual-count coordinate for Poisson entropy budgets and rate-entropy parametrizations of Gamma and Dirichlet counting channels connect model parameters to remaining uncertainty. The framework unifies distortion selection, compatible-channel construction, and optimality verification.

papers.title: A $\Theta(n)$-Multiplicative Improvement of the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound for Linear and Quantum Codes
papers.abstract: The Gilbert-Varshamov (GV) bound is a fundamental benchmark for the existence of error-correcting codes. For non-linear $q$-ary codes of code length $n$, its finite length form is known to admit a multiplicative improvement of order $\Theta(n)$. In contrast, for $q$-ary linear codes of arbitrary rates, the best previously known general improvement was only of order $\Theta(\sqrt n)$. This leaves open whether the algebraic constraint of linearity inherently prevents a linear-order refinement. We show that it does not. For every fixed prime power $q$ and relative distance $0<\delta<1-1/q$, we obtain a $\Theta(n)$-multiplicative improvement of the GV bound for $q$-ary linear codes of arbitrary rate, matching the corresponding result for nonlinear codes. Our proof is based on a simple change of viewpoint. Rather than requiring the initial random linear construction to contain no low-weight vectors, we allow $O(n)$ low-weight points, show that they are independent in the underlying projective space, and then eliminate all of them simultaneously at the cost of a single dimension. The key probabilistic ingredient is an exponential bound on nontrivial linear dependencies among low-weight vectors. We further show that this approach can be extended to quantum codes despite the symplectic self-orthogonality constraint. We obtain a $\Theta(n)$-multiplicative improvement of the quantum GV bound for every fixed $0<\delta<1-1/q^2$ satisfying $H_{q^2}(\delta)<1/2$. Thus, the same $\Theta(n)$ finite length improvement is applicable to both general linear structure and symplectic self-orthogonality.

papers.title: Optimized Mirabbasi-Martin Pulse Shaping Filter for Higher-Order Modulation in Zak-OTFS
papers.abstract: The performance of Zak-OTFS modulation depends critically on the delay-Doppler (DD) domain pulse shaping filter, which must support both accurate channel estimation and reliable data detection. Filters reported in the Zak-OTFS literature fall short in bit error rate (BER) performance for higher-order modulation due to sensitivity to model-free channel estimation errors and pilot-data interference. Motivated by this, in this paper, we introduce a separable two-dimensional Mirabbasi-Martin (MM) filter for Zak-OTFS and propose a filter coefficient optimization framework that minimizes the aggregate sidelobe energy while preserving the compact structure of the MM prototype. By trading exact Nyquist nulls for high localization, the optimized MM filter exhibits no sidelobes with the narrowest $-40$ dB DD domain pulsewidth compared to sinc, Gaussian, and GS pulses. This compactness of the optimized filter tightly confines the pilot energy within the pilot region of the embedded frame, ensuring that the full response is captured for model-free channel estimation while significantly reducing pilot-data interference. This yields both an improved estimation performance and a significantly improved BER performance for higher-order QAM. For the proposed filter, we derive closed-form expressions for the effective DD domain channel and the covariance of the receive-filtered noise, which drastically reduce simulation run times. Our simulation results demonstrate that the optimized MM filter achieves significantly better uncoded/coded BER performance for higher-order QAM compared to that of sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters. For example, for 64-QAM with M=32, N=48, rate-1/2 convolutional code, and TDL-A channel model with fractional DDs, the optimized MM filter achieves a coded BER of 3x10^{-4} at an E_b/N_0 of 40 dB, while the sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters exhibit error floors above 10^{-2}.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for Multiple-Access Channels --Part II : $\varepsilon$-Capacity Regions in the Mixed Finite-Alphabet Case
papers.abstract: In a nonergodic channel such as a slowly fading link, the channel law is drawn once and held fixed for the whole codeword, and the relevant performance measure is the $\varepsilon$-capacity. We study the $\varepsilon$-capacity regions of two-user mixed multiple-access channels (MACs) with finite alphabets, additive cost constraints and an arbitrary mixing measure. The direct parts are derived from a single information spectrum formula; the converse parts use, in addition, Fano's inequality and Ahlswede's strong converse applied to each component. Without knowledge of the realized component, we prove a single-letter inner bound for every $0\le\varepsilon<1$, in which one input serves all components; for $\varepsilon=0$ it is tight, and the capacity region is given by the essential infima of the component mutual informations. We prove a single-letter outer bound, the outage region, in which each component may use its own input; it holds with or without channel state information (CSI) at either terminal, and it is the $\varepsilon$-capacity region when the encoders know the component and the parameter space is countable. Both bounds coincide, in all four CSI scenarios, for well-ordered mixed MACs, which include degradedly ordered families and mixtures with a common optimal input, such as mixed additive MACs. Without CSI the outer bound can be strictly loose, and the no-CSI $\varepsilon$-capacity region for $0<\varepsilon<1$ remains open in general. Finally, we extend Ahlswede's strong converse to $K$ users with cost constraints and show that most of these results extend to $K$-user mixed MACs.

papers.title: Information Spectrum Methods for MUltiple-Access Channels--Part III : The Strong Converse in the $K$-User Gaussian Case
papers.abstract: This paper, Part III of a series, treats $K$-user multiple-access channels (MACs). Its starting point is a pair of fundamental lemmas, a random-coding lemma of Feinstein type and a converse lemma of Verd\'u--Han type, which are the $K$-user extensions of the two lemmas underlying Han's information spectrum approach to the general two-user MAC. From them we derive the capacity region of the general $K$-user MAC with cost constraint and show that it contains the polymatroid capacity region of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC. We then prove, by an elementary information spectrum calculation that adapts a diffuse--exceptional subspace decomposition used in recent second-order converses for the Gaussian MAC, that for every subset $\cS$ of users and every independent input satisfying the power constraints, the conditional information spectral-sup rate of the $K$-user Gaussian MAC does not exceed $\frac12\log(1+P_\cS/N)$, where $P_\cS$ is the total power of the users in $\cS$, with a probability bound that does not depend on the input. Consequently, the strong converse for the $K$-user Gaussian MAC, in the sense that the error probability tends to one for every rate tuple outside the capacity region, follows directly from the converse lemma, without the wringing technique and without hypothesis-testing meta-converses. This strong converse was first established by Fong and Tan, whose per-blocklength bounds yield it, through wringing and quantization. It is the key ingredient in the converse parts of the coding theorems for mixed Gaussian MACs in Part I, where the $\varepsilon$-strong converse would not suffice.

papers.title: Key Relay and Secure Network Coding: One-Shot Equivalence and Separation on Undirected Networks
papers.abstract: Motivated by quantum key distribution networks, we compare key relay protocols with secure network coding on the same undirected graph. In this comparison, we fix the finite field, terminal set, and wiretap family. Each edge supplies one independent uniform symbol to its endpoints for key relay, or carries one symbol once for network coding. The network code may choose its source terminal, edge orientations, and causal transmission order before execution. In this setting, the standard one-time-pad simulation readily converts every secure network code to key relay. We investigate the reverse conversion to linear network coding. For two terminals and a one-symbol key, arbitrary key relay is equivalent to scalar linear acyclic network coding over the prescribed field. The proof uses connectivity and flow conservation, related to the binary $st$-flow protocol. However, this equivalence fails in general when several terminals seek one common key. A doubled triangle separates key relay from acyclic coding but admits causal coding on a cyclic orientation. On the four-terminal complete graph, a linear key relay protocol over the ternary field withstands the three perfect-matching wiretap sets, whereas no linear causal network code distributes a source symbol of the same size, even with private randomness at every vertex and its use in decoding. We also establish a linear key relay normal form that removes interaction and private randomness and bounds public communication. All results concern one-shot feasibility with exact agreement and perfect secrecy.

papers.title: Quantum Telatar formula: fading quantum capacity of Haar-random multimode attenuators
papers.abstract: Cellular communication is done over an imperfectly predictable multimode environment, where the sender only knows about the distribution of possible intermode coupling and scattering a signal faces. It may thus seem surprising that such communication is efficient. Telatar proved that the sender's lack of exact knowledge about the channel, on average, does not significantly hinder multimode communication. As the number $N$ of modes increases at fixed signal-to-noise ratio, the average capacity of a classical multimode fading channel grows linearly in $N$, like that of $N$ decoupled single-mode channels. We study the quantum analogue in a Haar-random passive bosonic network and prove a similar scaling for unassisted quantum information transmission. Suppose that the sender drives a fixed fraction of the input modes and the receiver collects more than half of the output modes. Then the quantum capacity of such channels at zero temperature grows linearly with the number of modes at fixed photon number per mode, just like the classical capacity grows with the number of antennas. At nonzero temperature, the Haar-averaged coherent information of the isotropic thermal input bounds the capacity from below, and its value per mode converges to an integral against Wachter's law. We numerically identify positive achievable rates in models motivated by cryogenic microwave networks and room-temperature multimode fibers.

papers.title: Subadditivity and the failure of strong subadditivity in the Nichols--Wootters family of entropies
papers.abstract: We prove subadditivity for the Nichols--Wootters family of entropies interpolating between the von Neumann entropy and the subentropy, with all spectra evaluated in one common ambient dimension. Beyond the von Neumann entropy, equality holds exactly when at least one marginal is pure. This settles the subadditivity conjecture concerning subentropy. Every member except the von Neumann entropy fails strong subadditivity, already on a maximally entangled two-qubit state tensored with a mixed qubit. Its strong-subadditivity defect takes both signs on quantum Markov states. For a pure bipartite state tensored with an ancillary state, we identify the defect with a separately concave product gap and determine its exact maximum under rank constraints. For arbitrary bipartite states, we obtain an explicit lower bound in the marginal purities. For two-qubit states, we determine the optimal coefficient multiplying the product of the smaller marginal eigenvalues in every common ambient dimension, including the subentropy coefficient $1/3$. A positive representation by Haar averages of compressed matrix entropies gives the pinching inequality underlying these results and also yields entropy-gain bounds for unital quantum channels.As an application, each entropy equals the classical communication capacity retained after a specified isotropic partial projective measurement, at a prescribed average input state, even when entangled block encodings are allowed.
